descripcion: Principal AI Research Scientist: Designing Multi-Scale Intelligence for the Energy Transition Remote • Full-time • Three-year grant-funded term (renewable) Link to application: https://noteforms.com/forms/principal-ai-research-scientist-application-tgtkdo Ready to help shape the next frontier of AI by designing intelligent systems that reason across nested scales—from buildings to cities to nations—to accelerate the global energy transition. Open Earth Foundation (OEF) is a non-profit research and development organization building open digital infrastructure for planetary stewardship. We develop open digital infrastructure, AI systems, and data platforms that strengthen multi-stakeholder coordination and accelerate environmental protection, climate action, and Earth-system resilience. We’re a diverse, global team working remotely and collaborating with partners worldwide to make real change possible. With strong funding and a powerhouse team of innovators, we’re ready to tackle big challenges for a resilient Earth for generations to come and we need the planet’s brightest minds to help solve them! Your mission, should you choose to accept it: As the Principal AI Research Scientist for NEST at Open Earth Foundation, you will define the AI research architecture behind a new generation of intelligent systems for multi-scale energy-transition planning. You will set the research agenda, design the nested-agent and reasoning architectures that underpin the programme, and help shape its long-term scientific vision. NEST (Nested Energy System Transitions) is a three-year research programme funded by Schmidt Sciences through the Decarbonization and Energy Virtual Institute (DEVI) initiative. The programme is developing AI-agent architectures that connect existing energy models across nested spatial, temporal, and organizational scales, from buildings and cities to national systems, and from near-term operations to multi-decadal planning. The goal is to produce coherent energy-transition pathways by advancing both the intelligent systems and agentic research processes needed for cross-scale reasoning and model coupling. This is an architectural research role, not a production engineering role. You will design and validate new approaches, working closely with consortium Principal Investigators, Active Inference Scientists, and the Full-Stack AI Engineers who translate promising directions into robust systems. Success in this role could redefine how intelligent systems reason across interacting models, disciplines, and scales—well beyond climate and energy applications. This position is fully remote and international as our organization works across different time zones. This position is fully remote and international, full-time, and grant-funded for a three-year term with the possibility of renewal. Regular overlap with Central European and U.S. Pacific working hours required. Opportunities to participate in occasional in-person team gatherings. Priority will be given to applications submitted by August 14th. The following requirements describe our ideal candidate. If you don't meet some of the requirements, you're encouraged to apply anyway. Let us know if there is something missing and how we can work together to make it up. Essential Functions and Specific Duties: Set the AI research direction: Define and drive NEST’s agenda for agentic, probabilistic, and multi-scale intelligence across coupled models. Design nested intelligence: Co-design nested agents, advanced agent architectures, and the agentic research processes that make cross-scale coupling possible. Create coherent representations: Explore hierarchical agents, latent-state representations, world models, and uncertainty-aware methods that remain consistent across spatial, temporal, and organizational scales. Prototype and validate: Turn original research ideas into working prototypes and research instruments through hands-on experimentation and rapid iteration. Bridge research and production: Hand promising designs and coupling strategies to the Lead Full-Stack AI Engineer to harden into the production platform. Align with inference science: Partner with the Active Inference Scientist so the intelligence architecture and Bayesian inference layer—including factor graphs, message passing, and convergence—fit together. Set the scientific bar: Define standards for reproducibility, validation, posterior predictive checks, and comparison with established model couplings and benchmarks. Publish and represent the work: Shape NEST’s long-term scientific vision and communicate the research through publications, presentations, and external collaborations. Other: Actively participate in team building and culture-development activities at Open Earth Foundation. Contribute to an open, collaborative research culture grounded in rigor, curiosity, and shared purpose. Qualifications: PhD advancing the AI/ML field with a track record of original contributions in architectures, reasoning frameworks, or research methodologies—not only applications of existing models. Deep expertise in probabilistic reasoning, Bayesian methods, machine learning, or related approaches for uncertainty-aware AI systems. A record of turning ambitious ideas into rigorous research and impactful outcomes. Hands-on ability to translate research into working prototypes through experimentation and rapid iteration. descripcion: Description Why This Role A role that drives the business Company has a new GTM strategy — and Sales Operations is being re-built to support it. This role requires a candidate who will design and build annual targets and forecasting frameworks, BI infrastructure, territory, quota and capacity models — and own the process end-to-end. High visibility, real influence This role produces work that will be seen and used by Sales Leadership, executive leadership (including the CRO) and cross-functional teams. Analysis from this role will shape how the go-to-market organization makes decisions on pipeline, quota, investments and resource allocation. Broad scope with real ownership This role owns forecasting and reporting — but arguably more important are the analytics: territory design, customer segmentation, ICP definition, TAM analysis, and capacity and quota modeling. This role is expected to develop and connect these inputs into a consolidated picture of where the business is today and what is needed to grow. A Company That Takes Analytics Seriously This role reports to the VP of Sales Operations and will work alongside Sales Leadership. The expectation for the role is to leverage data and insights to influence decisions and drive outcomes across sales. Requirements Advanced English Analytical Modeling & Quantitative Depth Expert-level Excel — dynamic arrays, Power Query, complex nested formulas, and large dataset modeling; builds from scratch, not from templates Proven ability to build assumption-driven, scenario-based models with clearly documented inputs, auditable logic, and executive-ready outputs Hands-on Tableau dashboard development; experience with AI-augmented BI tools a strong plus Salesforce reporting and data extraction proficiency; SQL or similar query language a plus Strong command of GTM metrics: ACV, TCV, ARR, win rate, pipeline velocity, coverage ratios, and attainment curves Forecasting & Revenue Mechanics Deep familiarity with sales forecasting methodologies — pipeline coverage, weighted forecasts, stage-based probability, and bottoms-up/tops-down reconciliation Ability to connect bookings data to revenue recognition principles; partner to Finance / Delivery on bookings-to-revenue modeling Experience building capacity and quota coverage models with scenario-based outputs and clearly documented assumptions Communication & Influence Translates quantitative analysis into clear, action-oriented narratives for senior leadership Comfortable presenting to and influencing executive stakeholders in high-stakes settings Self-directed with strong organizational skills; manages competing priorities independently and drives work to completion Builds presentation materials and dashboards that meet executive-ready standards, in partnership with the VP of Sales Operations Required Experience & Education 6+ years of experience in an analytical, quantitative role with a track record of building structured models that drove real decisions Demonstrated experience documenting assumptions, building scenario-based models, and presenting findings to senior leadership Hands-on Tableau dashboard development experience Proficiency in Salesforce reporting and data management Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Business, or a related analytical field Backgrounds We Value Management consulting — especially commercial due diligence, GTM strategy, or sales force effectiveness work Revenue Operations or Sales Operations at a high-growth B2B or SaaS company where forecasting was taken seriously Corporate strategy or business operations at a data-driven company FP&A or financial planning with exposure to go-to-market or commercial modeling GTM analytics, business intelligence, or sales finance in a complex B2B environment MBA or advanced degree in a quantitative discipline a plus, but not required Job responsibilities Senior analytical leader within the Sales Operations team. This role owns the full spectrum of sales forecasting, pipeline reporting, territory and capacity modeling, and business intelligence — and is expected to bring both the technical depth and business judgment to analyze data that drive business decisions and outcomes. This is a hands-on role with broad ownership across teams. He will design and build the target & forecast frameworks, BI infrastructure, and capacity and quota models for the sales organization. Strong candidates will be equally comfortable developing a bottoms-up capacity model in Excel as they are presenting forecast assumptions to senior leadership. The ability to think in scenarios, document assumptions clearly, and deliver insights that drive action is essential. This role owns the development and build of all analytics, dashboards, and presentation materials in partnership with the VP of Sales Operations. The role will interact with Sales Leaders and cross-functional teams regularly and is expected to influence outcomes. Work product should be executive-ready — clear, well-structured, and suitable for senior audiences without significant rework. Essential Responsibilities Segmentation, Territories & TAM Define and maintain Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) — incorporating firmographic, behavioral, and performance data to guide targeting, segmentation, and go-to-market prioritization. Analyze the existing customer base and prospect universe to develop and refine segmentation — by industry vertical, region, company size, revenue tier, and buying behavior. Map segmentation outputs to total addressable market (TAM) data to identify whitespace, growth opportunities, and resource gaps. Build and maintain territory models that balance market potential, historical performance, and headcount capacity — recommending realignments as the business evolves. Partner with Sales Leadership on annual and mid-year territory assignments; maintain underlying models to support rapid scenario planning. Capacity & Quota Modeling Build and maintain detailed capacity models — incorporating headcount plans, ramp curves, productivity assumptions, attrition, and coverage ratios — to project achievable bookings targets. Develop bottoms-up and tops-down quota models that translate company-level bookings targets into rep, team, and regional allocations; clearly document all assumptions. Create scenario models (e.g., attainment curves, new hire ramp, segment mix shifts) to support executive planning cycles and mid-year adjustments. Monitor quota attainment and capacity utilization in-period; flag risks to plan and recommend corrective actions. Forecasting & Pipeline Management Own all bookings and pipeline forecasting — monthly, quarterly, and annual — with accountability for forecast accuracy. Build and maintain a structured, repeatable forecasting process; collect, validate, and reconcile rep and manager forecasts against pipeline data in Salesforce. Develop and publish weekly forecast packages for Sales Leadership and executive stakeholders, including pipeline health, coverage ratios, risk/upside flags, and trend analysis. Monitor pipeline movement, stage progression, and deal velocity weekly; surface actionable signals to Sales Leadership proactively. Partner with Finance to align bookings forecasts with revenue recognition models and establish shared reporting standards. Analytics, Dashboards & BI Design, build, and own Tableau dashboards, AI-powered BI tools, and executive-ready presentation materials — in partnership with the VP of Sales Operations — delivering real-time visibility into bookings performance, pipeline health, rep productivity, and revenue trends for Sales Leadership and cross-functional stakeholders. Develop a standardized suite of sales KPIs and operating metrics; automate reporting to eliminate manual processes and reduce time-to-insight. Conduct ad hoc analysis to answer strategic questions from Sales Leadership and the CRO — delivering clear, concise, and actionable outputs. Translate large, complex data sets into business narratives that drive decisions; present findings to senior audiences with confidence and clarity. Serve as the primary owner of sales data integrity — partner with Salesforce admins to enforce CRM hygiene and reporting standards. About CookUnity Food has lost its soul to modern convenience. And with it, it has lost the power to nourish, inspire, and connect us. So in 2018, CookUnity was founded as the first-of-its-kind platform that connects the world with the source of truly great food: chefs. Today, CookUnity delivers 50 million meals a year from the industry’s best chefs to homes all over the country. Fresh. Ready-to-eat. And crafted with the passion that nourishes body and soul. Unwilling to stop there, CookUnity is expanding beyond delivery to become an ever-innovating marketplace focused on our singular mission: empower Chefs to nourish the world. If that mission has you hungry in more ways than one, you’ve found the right job posting. The Role CookUnity is looking for a Senior Data Analyst, B2B to own and scale analytics across our growing B2B business. Our B2B organization serves customers through multiple business models—including Corporate, Smart Fridge, and Healthcare—each with distinct go-to-market motions, customer journeys, and economics. You will build the analytics foundation that helps us understand how these businesses are performing, where our biggest growth opportunities are, and how we can scale them efficiently. You’ll partner closely with Sales, Partnerships, Sales Enablement, Marketing, Finance, and B2B leadership to connect the dots from pipeline generation and conversion through customer performance, retention, revenue, and profitability. This role is the connective tissue between the B2B business and CookUnity’s core Data team. Today, B2B analytics are spread across multiple tools—Salesforce, Tableau, Hex, and standalone dashboards—with no single owner consolidating them into a coherent, executive-ready view. You will be that owner. You’ll translate what B2B leadership needs to see into what the Data Engineering team needs to build, and ensure that every metric the business runs on is accurate, consistent, and available without manual effort. This is a highly visible role for someone who enjoys bringing structure to ambiguous business problems, building reliable metrics and reporting from the ground up, and translating data into recommendations that directly influence commercial decisions. What You’ll Do Own the analytics strategy for CookUnity’s B2B business, developing the reporting infrastructure, executive-ready dashboards, and analytical frameworks needed to understand and accelerate growth across Corporate, Smart Fridge, Healthcare, and emerging B2B opportunities (e.g., Airbnb, partnerships). Build an authoritative, single-source-of-truth view of B2B business health—clean data, executive-level visibility, one place leadership goes for the numbers. Partner with B2B leadership to translate business objectives into measurable KPIs and data models that connect the full commercial funnel—from lead generation and pipeline through conversion, activation, revenue, retention, and expansion. Partner with Sales, Partnerships, Sales Enablement, and Marketing to analyze pipeline health, conversion rates, sales velocity, win/loss patterns, deal velocity by stage, and other drivers of commercial productivity. Identify opportunities to improve how we acquire, prioritize, and grow B2B customers. Build the attribution layer that connects marketing spend to SQLs, pipeline created, and ARR won—by channel and by vertical. Partner with Finance and B2B leadership on forecasting and planning, translating pipeline and customer trends into forward-looking views of revenue and business performance, and helping explain gaps between plan and actuals. Own the data inputs for the Board-ready standard metric pack—including ARR bridge (opening → new → expansion → contraction → churn → closing), profitability trend, retention cohorts, stage-weighted pipeline, and efficiency metrics—per pod and consolidated. Develop a deep understanding of B2B business economics, including revenue, retention, expansion, order behavior, margins, and unit economics. Surface the segments, channels, ICPs (Ideal Customer Profiles), and customer profiles that create the greatest long-term value. Build LTV and CAC analysis at the B2B level to start, with increasing granularity by pod and ICP over time. Build the analytical frameworks needed to compare performance across B2B pods and business models, recognizing that success may look different across Corporate, Smart Fridge, and Healthcare while creating a common language and standard scorecard for leadership. Define what green/yellow/red looks like for each pod’s key metrics. Develop and maintain automated dashboards and reporting that give commercial teams and leadership timely visibility into pipeline, revenue, customer health, and key business drivers—reducing manual reporting and increasing confidence in the numbers. Consolidate today’s scattered reporting (Salesforce, Tableau, Hex, standalone tools) into a unified, reliable analytics layer. Go beyond reporting to diagnose what is driving performance. Proactively identify trends, risks, and opportunities and translate them into clear recommendations for Sales, Partnerships, Marketing, Finance, and B2B leadership. Own analyses like: retention by cohort with largest-account exclusion, pipeline movement waterfalls (added/advanced/slipped/lost), Healthcare funnel conversion (applications submitted → approved → contracting), and ICP-level performance tracking. Serve as the connective tissue between the B2B business and CookUnity’s core Data and Analytics Engineering teams. Translate B2B business requirements into data modeling and infrastructure needs. Partner with Analytics Engineering and Data Engineering to improve B2B data foundations—ensuring critical commercial and operational data (Salesforce ingestion, ad platform integrations, pricing logic, coupon attribution) is modeled consistently, accurately, and at the right level of granularity. Drive the B2B data alignment roadmap and ensure the Data team’s build priorities reflect the business’s most pressing analytical needs. Turn complex analyses into clear, compelling business stories. Present insights and recommendations to senior stakeholders—including Board-level presentations—in a way that makes the “so what” obvious and helps teams make faster, better decisions. Qualifications 5+ years of experience in analytics, ideally supporting B2B, enterprise sales, revenue operations, commercial strategy, or a similar go-to-market organization. Advanced proficiency in SQL, with the ability to independently explore, transform, validate, and analyze large and sometimes imperfect datasets. Strong understanding of B2B and commercial metrics, such as pipeline, funnel conversion, sales velocity, win rates, revenue, retention, expansion, account performance, and unit economics. Experience building dashboards, recurring business reporting, and executive-ready metric packs that become reliable sources of truth for commercial teams and leadership. Strong analytical problem-solving skills and the ability to take an ambiguous business question, structure it, identify the right data, and turn the analysis into a recommendation. Experience partnering with Sales, Finance, Marketing, Partnerships, Revenue Operations, or other commercial stakeholders, with an understanding of how analytics can influence both strategic and day-to-day decisions. Experience with business intelligence platforms such as Tableau, Looker, or equivalent. Strong communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to translate complex analyses into concise insights for both technical and non-technical audiences, including Board-level presentations. Excellent English, both written and spoken, given our U.S. presence and cross-functional collaboration. Comfortable operating with high autonomy in a fast-paced environment, balancing recurring reporting needs with deeper strategic analyses and proactively identifying where analytics can create value. Preferred Experience working with CRM and sales data, particularly Salesforce or similar platforms. Experience with revenue forecasting, sales capacity/productivity analysis, customer segmentation, or account-level economics. Experience analyzing businesses with multiple B2B go-to-market motions or customer segments (e.g., enterprise sales, self-serve/kiosk, marketplace, healthcare payer relationships). Familiarity with ETL, data warehousing, and data modeling concepts; experience with tools such as dbt and Snowflake is a plus. Experience working in a high-growth startup, marketplace, food-tech, or operationally complex business. Familiarity with connecting commercial data to financial and operational outcomes, rather than analyzing the sales funnel in isolation. Experience consolidating analytics across multiple disconnected tools and data sources into a unified reporting layer. Exposure to healthcare or regulated-industry sales cycles (RFPs, credentialing, payer contracting) is a plus. Building the Future of Open Finance Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. Before you apply, we encourage you to explore our culture page to understand what drives us and how we work. The team Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. We’re looking for a Data Analyst, Product to join our team remotely. The #1 goal of this role is to turn complex data into clear, actionable insights that improve user experience, support the development of new features, deepen engagement, and help leadership make high-impact product decisions. You’ll own end-to-end data management from production-grade pipelines and dbt models to dashboards and metric frameworks for the Pro product team. You'll define north star metrics from the ground up, drive experimentation infrastructure through A/B testing and causal inference, and translate results into clear product recommendations. We're actively building a culture where AI tooling is part of how we work, from LLM-augmented pipelines to GenAI-assisted workflows, and we're looking for people who are excited to grow alongside that. Beyond technical expertise, success in this role depends on being a true business partner who combines data-driven insights with deep knowledge of client retention funnels and user behaviour. You bring experience from environments where data quality has real consequences and where you've had to build the infrastructure, not just use it. The opportunity Operate as a full-stack data analyst within the Pro team, owning your domain completely while collaborating closely with colleagues across the pod. Own the design and evolution of dashboards, north star metrics and analytical frameworks that drive decisions at the highest level of the business. Build and maintain data infrastructure at scale, from scalable dbt models and production pipelines to full-funnel reporting that powers cross-functional teams. Lead experimentation across the Product domain by designing and owning A/B testing frameworks, applying causal inference techniques and turning results into clear, confident recommendations that influence product strategy. Influence technical direction across the data team, contributing to how we build, what we prioritise and how we raise the bar on data quality and engineering standards. Embed AI tooling into your workflow in ways that have tangible business impact, including LLM-augmented pipelines and GenAI-assisted analytics workflows. Deliver insights through clear, data-driven storytelling to technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership. What You Bring 7+ years of experience in data analytics or analytics engineering, ideally within fintech, payments, financial market or crypto where data quality and scale are non-negotiable. You have hands-on experience with advanced trading products and solutions in equities, crypto, or other assets. You either have a professional background working within financial markets or on a trading desk, or you are a professional trader. Hands-on experience building and owning production data pipelines, with strong familiarity with dbt and Airflow or equivalent orchestration tools. Full mastery of SQL including complex joins, CTEs and analytical functions, alongside strong Python proficiency for pipeline development and analysis. Hands-on experience designing and running A/B tests and experimentation frameworks, with the ability to apply causal inference techniques and translate results into clear growth recommendations. Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional data initiatives from design to delivery, with measurable business outcomes you can point to. Strong communicator who can simplify complex data ideas for both technical and non-technical audiences. A degree in a field emphasising analytical rigour such as software engineering, economics or a hard science. Based in Canada, the US, the UK or the EU and fluent in English. Walk through your approach. Reference check + Offer 🎁 What You Get 🏡 Fully Remote. Work from anywhere. 📈 Equity share. Own a piece of what you're building. 💵 Profit sharing. titulo: Full Stack Engineer for VC-Backed AI Startup
descripcion: ABOUT INTRIQ Intriq turns a client's disorganised data room into deal-ready insight. We build the platform that lets accounting and audit teams process financial documents at machine speed without losing the rigour a human review demands. Every output is derived solely from the client's own data, nothing external. THE ROLE You will build the platform that does it, from the React workspace auditors touch every day, down through the async Python pipelines that read and reason over financial documents. You will work across three repositories: QNextDash (frontend), QInsights (API and pipeline backend) and QCLI (internal tooling), shipping features end to end rather than staying on one side of a spec. This is not a maintenance role. You will be one of the first engineers shaping how the async document pipeline, the API contracts and the infrastructure scale as we take on larger clients and heavier document volumes. WHAT YOU WILL ACTUALLY DO • Build across the stack. A Next.js workspace view one week, the FastAPI endpoint and Postgres schema behind it the next. • Design and harden async workflows: document ingestion, markdown conversion, LLM-based extraction and multi-step review pipelines that stay correct under concurrency and partial failure. • Own services from Terraform up. Provision the Fargate task or Lambda, wire the CI/CD pipeline, and watch it in CloudWatch once it is live. • Work directly with data. Shape Postgres schemas, write the queries behind reporting and audit trails, and keep every pipeline output traceable back to its source document. • Make architecture calls with the founding team. At this size, the person who writes the code decides how it is structured. THE STACK Frontend: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, TanStack Query, Zustand, Tailwind API and pipeline: FastAPI, Pydantic v2, asyncpg, PostgreSQL 17, AWS Lambda, Bedrock and Claude Infrastructure: AWS Fargate, AWS Lambda, Terraform, Docker, GitHub Actions, CloudWatch, Cognito WHAT WE NEED • Proven full-stack experience. Comfortable moving from a React and TypeScript interface to a Python API to the database underneath, not fluent in one layer only. • Strong TypeScript and Python, with FastAPI or a comparable async Python framework in production. • Real experience designing async workflows and APIs. You can reason about concurrency, retries and partial failure, not just the happy path. • Solid PostgreSQL. Schema design, query performance and migrations, not an ORM you have never looked past. • Working knowledge of microservices and the trade-offs of splitting against consolidating services. • Some data engineering or ML exposure. Building or consuming data pipelines, working with LLM-based extraction, or shipping features that depend on model output. • DevOps fluency. CI/CD and AWS in practice: Fargate, Lambda, Terraform. You ship your own infrastructure changes rather than handing them off. • Startup pace, said plainly: small team, direct ownership, fast iteration, decisions made by whoever is closest to the problem. You will ship in your first week and own real production surface within your first month. USEFUL, NOT ESSENTIAL • Experience in fintech, audit or accounting software, where correctness and traceability matter as much as speed. • Exposure to security and compliance for AI systems, and familiarity with compliance tooling such as Sprinto. Intriq is SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certified, and the standard shapes how we build. • Spanish and English both used day to day. Portuguese is a bonus. HOW WE WORK • Remote, based in Argentina. The team is distributed and works to US hours, so expect a US calendar and overlap with the US working day. • Small by design. A handful of engineers, no layers between you and the founders. • Secure by default. Client data stays in the client's own environment. No cross-client model training. US-hosted models only. THE PROCESS Three conversations: an intro, a live coding interview with the engineering team, and an architecture discussion with the founding team. We read every application and aim to run the process inside two weeks. If you have not heard from us within two weeks, please take it as a no. If you have shipped something you are proud of that touches this stack, put that at the top of your application rather than writing a cover letter. Show more Show less

His background reflects the deep technical curiosity, intensity, and builder mindset that defines MixRank’s culture. We’re looking for passionate individuals for whom programming is not just a job, but something they love to do. We’re obsessed with computers, programming, big data, databases, compilers, hardware, math, data science, and the internet. If this sounds like you, please apply to join our team. We’ll cater the role to the areas that best match your interests. Our codebase is friendly to new contributors. You’ll have a fully functional development environment within hours, and many engineers start contributing quickly. Deployments to production happen multiple times per day and finish in less than 2 minutes. Effectively all of our codebase is written in Python, Rust, SQL, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Nix. The core technologies you’ll need familiarity with to be productive are Python, PostgreSQL, Linux, and Git. Beneficial experience includes PostgreSQL, Python, Rust, Linux, TypeScript, Nix, frontend/backend web development, and data mining. Unlike a typical startup where you might spend half your time in meetings and the other half fixing Jira tickets, at MixRank you’ll work on difficult technical problems that help you grow as an engineer. What we value in engineers We’re especially interested in engineers who are passionate programmers beyond their day-to-day work. This might mean contributing to open-source projects, building hobby projects, experimenting with new programming languages, writing tools for yourself, or exploring technical ideas simply because they’re interesting. Many of the strongest engineers we’ve worked with are self-starters: people who teach themselves new things, follow their curiosity, and enjoy solving difficult problems independently. Experience with functional programming languages such as Haskell, OCaml, Lisp, Clojure, F#, or Scheme can be a strong signal of that curiosity, though it is not required. Because MixRank is fully remote and async, we look for people who are comfortable taking ownership, communicating clearly in writing, and making progress without needing constant supervision. You do not need to come from a traditional background or have experience with every technology we use. What matters most is that you genuinely enjoy programming, like learning deeply, and are motivated by hard technical problems. How you’ll ramp up We don’t believe in a one-size-fits-all onboarding plan. At MixRank, we hire people, not job titles, and every engineer brings a different background, pace, and set of strengths. If programming is something you genuinely love, we’ll support you as you get acquainted with our codebase, systems, and development workflow. Some engineers begin contributing meaningful changes very quickly; others spend more time learning the architecture, asking questions, and building context before taking on larger work. Both paths are welcome. Our goal is to help you become confident and productive in a way that fits you. You’ll have access to experienced teammates, a friendly codebase, and a development environment designed to help new contributors get started quickly. Mentorship and support If you’re earlier in your engineering career, you won’t be expected to understand everything on day one. You’ll be supported by experienced engineers as you learn the codebase, ask questions, review technical decisions, and build confidence working on complex systems. That support may include code reviews, architecture walkthroughs, pair debugging, and regular technical deep-dives into areas such as our distributed file system, crawling infrastructure, data pipelines, PostgreSQL scaling, and deployment workflow. We still value self-starters who enjoy learning independently, especially in a remote async environment. But independent does not mean unsupported. If you’re curious, persistent, and genuinely passionate about programming, we’ll help you grow into meaningful technical ownership over time. descripcion: About Atacana Atacana Group, Inc. is a global competitive strategy and intelligence consulting organization focused on the healthcare industry. We build and operate our own AI-powered intelligence platform, Avizum, it is currently used daily by professionals at large pharmaceutical companies. This role sits on that product team. Why join our fast-growing team? • Build real AI, not demos. AI systems running in production against proprietary data — with real users, real SLAs and real feedback loops. • Work that matters. The decisions our platform informs shape how treatments are developed, positioned and brought to patients who need them. • Results driven. We measure output, not when you work. Flexible hours let us schedule our days so that we do our best work without missing out on life’s important moments. • Freedom of location. 100% remote work. We are a globally distributed team, so we can work wherever we are happiest. • Diverse and global team. Our team members are located across 4 continents and 15+ countries. • Growth mindset. Atacana is a learning organization. We stay close to the latest research and tools, share what we learn, and expect everyone to keep leveling up. The role in one paragraph We are building the next generation of our platform. This role is accountable for the data it runs on: acquiring content — increasingly including audio and video — from a large and growing set of external sources, extracting structure from it reliably, and delivering it into downstream services with the quality, freshness and provenance our clients expect. It is primarely a hands-on engineering role with real architectural ownership, working alongside AI/ML, backend, data and infrastructure engineers. Stack. Python-centred and cloud-native: asynchronous services, containers and orchestration, relational and specialised data stores, and a mix of commercial and self-hosted language models. What you’ll own You will be building the system that turns the open, messy, uncooperative web data into a corpus that pharma executives, healthcare professionals, patients and researchers can trust and cite. • Own the crawler and extraction fleet. Design, scale and operate a large portfolio of crawlers and extractors across many heterogeneous external sources — scheduling, politeness and rate limits, incremental crawling, deduplication, and full provenance from raw artefact to published record. You will shape this system from architecture down to the code. • Keep extraction alive as the web moves. Sources restructure and paginate differently. Build the monitoring, alerting and self-healing that catches silent breakage. Drive the time from breakage to fix toward zero. It is an adversarial, always-changing problem, which is what makes it interesting. • Turn any format into structured data. HTML, PDFs, tables and images, and increasingly audio and video. Combine deterministic parsing with model-based extraction where it earns its place — structured outputs, cost control and human review where accuracy demands it — and measure the accuracy of both. • Own data quality as SLOs. Coverage, freshness, completeness and duplication as measured, alerted thresholds — not as anecdotes. Build the contracts and validation that stop bad data reaching downstream consumers, and set the standard the rest of the company trusts by default. • Ship changes on evidence, not vibes. Stand up evaluation harnesses, golden datasets, regression suites and tracing, so that every model, prompt and parser change is a measured improvement rather than a hopeful one. • Own the data platform end to end. Boundaries, contracts, data ownership, failure modes and migration paths; pipelines that are event-driven, idempotent, resumable, observable and graceful under partial failure or provider outage. Containers, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, cost and latency budgets, tenant isolation and data security are part of the job, not someone else’s. Write the design docs and defend the trade-offs. • Make spoken content first-class. Acquire and process audio and video at scale: transcription, speaker attribution, alignment of transcripts to source media, and extraction of the substance from long recordings. Conference talks, panels, and briefings that are effectively invisible today become part of the corpus because you made them so. What we expect at this level Beyond delivery, we expect you to raise the bar of the team: review code and designs, mentor engineers, and translate ambiguous business intent into a technical plan. Your influence should outlast any single system you build here. What we’re looking for If you meet most of the essentials below and are missing one or two, we would still like to hear from you. Data extraction & crawling at scale Essential •     Has built and operated a non-trivial crawler fleet — hundreds of sources — over a sustained period, not a one-off scraping project. •     Practical experience of the hard parts: politeness and rate limiting, session and cookie handling, proxy and IP management, pagination and incremental crawling, change detection, retry semantics, and rendering JavaScript-heavy pages reliably. •     Treats parser drift as a first-class engineering problem: schema and selector versioning, contract tests against fixtures, canary sources, and alerting on volume, freshness and null-rate anomalies rather than on exceptions alone. •     Document and content extraction: HTML-to-text normalisation, PDF parsing, tables, boilerplate removal, language detection, near-duplicate detection and content canonicalisation across syndicated sources. •     Backfill and reprocessing strategies for when extraction logic changes retroactively, including lineage that survives a reprocess. •     Working awareness of robots.txt, terms of use, licensed-content restrictions and the difference between what is technically possible and what we are permitted to do. In our industry, where data came from matters as much as what it says. Also valuable •     Audio and video processing at scale: speech-to-text pipelines (self-hosted or API-based), speaker diarisation, chunking and timestamping of long recordings, handling accents and poor audio, media transcoding and storage cost management — with a clear view of transcription accuracy as a measured quantity rather than an assumption. •     OCR for scanned or image-only sources. Software engineering & architecture Essential •     7+ years building and operating production software, including meaningful time owning architecture rather than only implementing it. •     Expert-level Python: async/await, typing, testing discipline, packaging, profiling. Strong API design (FastAPI or equivalent) and clean service boundaries. •     Demonstrable experience decomposing a system: modular monolith vs. microservices, contract and schema evolution, backwards-compatible migrations, and decommissioning legacy components without downtime. •     Comfortable writing architecture decision records and defending trade-offs in front of both engineers and non-technical stakeholders. Distributed systems Essential •     Solid fundamentals: idempotency, at-least-once vs. exactly-once delivery, retries and backoff, backpressure, poison messages, ordering, eventual consistency, distributed locks, partial failure. •     Hands-on with message brokers and task or workflow orchestration frameworks. •     Containers and orchestration in production: autoscaling, resource limits, health and readiness, rollout strategies, debugging a live incident. •     A relational database at scale — indexing, query plans, partitioning, connection pooling — and practical experience with multi-tenant data isolation. •     Observability as a habit: structured logging, metrics, distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry), SLOs and on-call ownership. Also valuable •     Experience with a vector database, and ideally a graph database. Applied AI Essential •     Real, hands-on delivery of LLM-based systems to production — not prototypes.
